capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. Measures local plan/endpoint differences; does not establish closed-loop settling or causal attribution. Requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.
capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

attribution.reason: Observed failure mode rather than a cause assignment: the maximum and terminal recorded tip speeds inside the 0.05 s window (1.5810152739742807 m/s and 0.6351726092425104 m/s) both exceed the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit while the position error is already inside 0.01 m, so the speed criterion could not be satisfied at any sampled point of the window even though position tracked well.

The recorded weights (terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_weight 5.0 versus tracking_weight 1.0) are consistent with a speed-light objective, but raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance: no cost contributions or scaling are retained, and no braking counterfactual has been run, so this candidate cannot be separated from plan-selection/horizon effects or from backend-model mismatch when they predict the same endpoint.

Recorded effective horizon fell 8 -> 1 control intervals across updates 27-34 and 34 of 35 updates ended with User_Requested_Stop against a single Solve_Succeeded, which is compatible with budget-limited plan selection; however the displayed updates recorded plan_accepted=true and the recorded error still decreased, and per-iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained, so this cannot be ranked against objective weighting or model mismatch.

Recorded one-step endpoints agree with matched measured endpoints within 0.0006-0.0077 m in tip position at sampled updates while velocity vector-difference norms reach 0.021-0.153 m/s, but the measured velocity is a deterministic reconstruction (J_site(q_backend) @ qdot_backend) while the predicted quantity is the recorded accepted first-step endpoint velocity, so part of the difference may be definitional; a 10 ms projected-state probe cannot explain an entire settling failure and no closed-loop replay exists.

The recorded 35 deadline misses and mean update wall time of 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period describe wall-clock scheduling of synchronous controller calls; under the host scheduling contract those calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so wall latency cannot itself be the mechanism of the physical settling failure (it remains relevant only as a possible contributor to truncated optimization, the plan-selection candidate).

request_content.question: Open question (no predetermined root cause): Given that terminal reach succeeded (reach_passed=true, handle f6be7b6a22b85; terminal_error_m=0.007642608585867386, handle f43a69b8c4da2, within reach_tolerance_m=0.01, handle f9e0cdc61f6d7) yet sampled secondary settling failed (sampled_settling_passed=false, handle fd03a5c6cee0f) against settling criteria position_limit_m=0.01 (handle f614ca2ba852e), speed_limit_m_s=0.02 (handle f01b97ab32ab4) over window_s=0.05 (handle f6382c260ba25), why did the tip not settle inside the window despite the small terminal position error? Recorded context: terminal_speed_m_s=0.6351726092425104 (handle f81b1dbe1d67b) still exceeds the settling speed limit; late_max_error_m=0.05813810428573256 (handle ff47840769a24) and late_max_speed_m_s=1.5810152739742807 (handle f141a00f08e6f) are the recorded late-window extremes; deadline_misses=35 (handle f3e59cefcd307) with mean_update_s=17.075238151415917 s (handle f5e0c39558a9c) against control_period_s=0.01 s (handle fd49845c3b95b), stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop=34 (handle f43420decaa95) and Solve_Succeeded=1 (handle f569f5a2f1f35), configured horizon=10 (handle f775debbc81c6), and prediction-dominated weighting (tracking_weight=1.0 vs velocity_weight/terminal_velocity_weight=0.0001, terminal_weight=5.0, holding_tip_speed_weight=0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.0). Which competing mechanisms best explain the failed settling: slow terminal approach not being braked within the short window (e.g. weak tip-speed/braking weighting relative to position tracking), per-update plan selection / selected-iteration and effective-horizon behavior across the 35 updates, repeated deadline misses inflating update latency, or residual backend-model mismatch between the one-step prediction and the measured backend motion? I ask for a bounded comparison of these candidates, not a dominant-cause verdict.
